title: Strange answers to the psychopath test
speaker: Jon Ronson

sentences.en: Translator: Timothy Covell Reviewer: Morton Bast The story starts: I was at a friend's house,
sentences.zh: 故事的开头是这样的：我在一个朋友家里

sentences.en: and she had on her shelf a copy of the DSM manual, which is the manual of mental disorders.
sentences.zh: 在她的架子上有一本《DSM手册》就是《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》

sentences.en: It lists every known mental disorder. And it used to be, back in the '50s, a very slim pamphlet.
sentences.zh: 它列举了所有已知的精神疾病而在50年代的时候，它还是本苗条的小册子

sentences.en: And then it got bigger and bigger and bigger, and now it's 886 pages long.
sentences.zh: 然后一步一步被增加成大胖子现在已经有886页厚了

sentences.en: And it lists currently 374 mental disorders.
sentences.zh: 目前手册列举了374种精神疾病

sentences.en: So I was leafing through it, wondering if I had any mental disorders, and it turns out I've got 12.
sentences.zh: 所以我大致翻阅了一下好奇我是否有任何精神疾病结果显示我得了12种

sentences.en: (Laughter) I've got generalized anxiety disorder, which is a given.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我得了广泛性焦虑症这是与生俱来的

sentences.en: I've got nightmare disorder, which is categorized if you have recurrent dreams of being pursued or declared a failure, and all my dreams involve people chasing me down the street going, "You're a failure!"
sentences.zh: 我还得了梦魇症这是根据分类得来的只要你周期性地梦见被追逐或者被宣判失败而我的梦里都有人在街道上追赶我向我叫道,"你太失败了"

sentences.en: (Laughter) I've got parent-child relational problems, which I blame my parents for.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我还有亲子关系问题这得归咎于我父母（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) I'm kidding. I'm not kidding.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑的，我还真没开玩笑

sentences.en: I'm kidding. And I've got malingering. And I think it's actually quite rare to have both malingering and generalized anxiety disorder, because malingering tends to make me feel very anxious.
sentences.zh: 好吧，开玩笑的我还得了诈病症我觉得同时拥有诈病症和广泛性焦虑症这并不是很常见因为诈病症会让我觉得非常焦虑

sentences.en: Anyway, I was looking through this book, wondering if I was much crazier than I thought I was, or maybe it's not a good idea to diagnose yourself with a mental disorder if you're not a trained professional, or maybe the psychiatry profession has a kind of strange desire
sentences.zh: 总之我浏览了这本书惊讶我比我想象中还要不正常又或许给自己诊断精神病并不是一个很好的想法如果你不是一个受过培训的专家又或许精神病学专家有一种怪癖

sentences.en: to label what's essentially normal human behavior as a mental disorder.
sentences.zh: 想要将正常的人类行为定义为精神疾病

sentences.en: I didn't know which of these was true, but I thought it was kind of interesting, and I thought maybe I should meet a critic of psychiatry to get their view, which is how I ended up having lunch with the Scientologists.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这哪些是真的但我觉得还蛮有趣的然后我想我应该和一个精神病学评论家见一面看看他有什么想法所以我就和一个科学论派学者共进午餐

sentences.en: (Laughter) It was a man called Brian, who runs a crack team of Scientologists who are determined to destroy psychiatry wherever it lies.
sentences.zh: 他叫Brian他管理着一个一流的科学论派团队同时也下定决心捣毁所有的精神医学

sentences.en: They're called the CCHR. And I said to him, "Can you prove to me that psychiatry is a pseudo-science that can't be trusted?"
sentences.zh: 他们被称为公民人权委员会（CCHR）我就跟他说,"你能向我证明精神医学是一门不值得信任的伪科学吗？”

sentences.en: And he said, "Yes, we can prove it to you."
sentences.zh: 然后他说，“可以，我证明给你看。”我又问，“怎么证明？”

sentences.en: And I said, "How?" And he said, "We're going to introduce you to Tony."
sentences.zh: 他说，“我打算介绍Tony给你认识。”

sentences.en: And I said, "Who's Tony?" And he said, "Tony's in Broadmoor."
sentences.zh: 我问，“谁是Tony？"他说，“Tony现在在布罗德莫。”

sentences.en: Now, Broadmoor is Broadmoor Hospital. It used to be known as the Broadmoor Asylum for the Criminally Insane.
sentences.zh: 布罗德莫，就是布罗德莫精神病院过去被称为精神病犯人的庇护所

sentences.en: It's where they send the serial killers, and the people who can't help themselves.
sentences.zh: 连环杀手就是被送到那里的还有那些无法自控的人

sentences.en: And I said to Brian, "Well, what did Tony do?"
sentences.zh: 我又问Brian，“Tony干过什么事？”

sentences.en: And he said, "Hardly anything. He beat someone up or something, and he decided to fake madness to get out of a prison sentence.
sentences.zh: 他说，“基本什么也没干他好像打了人还是其他什么事然后他决定装疯以此逃过牢狱之灾

sentences.en: But he faked it too well, and now he's stuck in Broadmoor and nobody will believe he's sane.
sentences.zh: 但他装得太像了，现在就在那里出不来了但没人相信他是正常的

sentences.en: Do you want us to try and get you into Broadmoor to meet Tony?"
sentences.zh: 你想让我们把你弄进去和Tony见面吗？”

sentences.en: So I said, "Yes, please." So I got the train to Broadmoor.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，“嗯，劳烦你了。”所以我踏上了前往布罗德莫精神病院的列车

sentences.en: I began to yawn uncontrollably around Kempton Park, which apparently is what dogs also do when anxious, they yawn uncontrollably.
sentences.zh: 我开始控制不住在坎普顿公园附近打哈欠显然，当狗在焦虑的时候也会情不自禁地打哈欠

sentences.en: And we got to Broadmoor. And I got taken through gate after gate after gate after gate into the wellness center, which is where you get to meet the patients.
sentences.zh: 之后就到了布罗德莫精神病院然后我又不停地穿过一道又一道又一道的大门这才进到健康中心那儿在那里你才能和病人会面

sentences.en: It looks like a giant Hampton Inn. It's all peach and pine and calming colors.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像大型的汉普顿酒店到处都是桃子菠萝和让人宁静的颜色

sentences.en: And the only bold colors are the reds of the panic buttons.
sentences.zh: 唯一比较大胆的颜色则是应急按钮上的红色

sentences.en: And the patients started drifting in. And they were quite overweight and wearing sweatpants, and quite docile-looking.
sentences.zh: 然后病人开始挪进来他们看起来很笨重，穿着宽松的裤子倒是挺温顺的样子

sentences.en: And Brian the Scientologist whispered to me, "They're medicated," which, to the Scientologists, is like the worst evil in the world, but I'm thinking it's probably a good idea.
sentences.zh: 科学论派学者Brian低声跟我说他们这是服药后的效果对于科学论派的人来说，这简直就是最残忍的魔鬼我倒不觉得是件坏事（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) And then Brian said, "Here's Tony."
sentences.zh: 然后Brian说，“Tony来了。”

sentences.en: And a man was walking in. And he wasn't overweight, he was in very good physical shape.
sentences.zh: 然后有个男人走了进来他看起来并不笨重，身材还挺不错

sentences.en: And he wasn't wearing sweatpants, he was wearing a pinstripe suit.
sentences.zh: 也没有穿宽松的裤子他穿着带有细条纹的西服

sentences.en: And he had his arm outstretched like someone out of The Apprentice.
sentences.zh: 他张开双臂像《飞黄腾达》里的人一样

sentences.en: He looked like a man who wanted to wear an outfit that would convince me that he was very sane.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像是想在着装方面显得得体的人这样似乎会让我相信他是正常人

sentences.en: And he sat down. And I said, "So is it true that you faked your way in here?"
sentences.zh: 然后他坐下来我说，“你是在这里装疯的对吧？”

sentences.en: And he said, "Yep. Yep. Absolutely. I beat someone up when I was 17.
sentences.zh: 他说，“对，绝对是。我在17岁的时候把别人打伤了

sentences.en: And I was in prison awaiting trial, and my cellmate said to me, 'You know what you have to do?
sentences.zh: 之后在监狱里等待审判我的狱友跟我说你知道你得做些什么吗

sentences.en: Fake madness. Tell them you're mad, you'll get sent to some cushy hospital.
sentences.zh: 装疯告诉他们你疯了，你就会被送到某间舒适的医院

sentences.en: Nurses will bring you pizzas, you'll have your own PlayStation.'"
sentences.zh: 护士会给你带来比萨饼你会有自己的PS游戏机。”

sentences.en: I said, "Well, how did you do it?" He said, "Well, I asked to see the prison psychiatrist.
sentences.zh: 我又说，“那你是怎么做的？”他说，“我要求去见监狱里的精神病专家

sentences.en: And I'd just seen a film called 'Crash,' in which people get sexual pleasure from crashing cars into walls.
sentences.zh: 而且我又看过《冲击效应》这部电影电影里的人用车去撞墙以获得性快感

sentences.en: So I said to the psychiatrist, 'I get sexual pleasure from crashing cars into walls.'"
sentences.zh: 所以我跟精神病专家说我通过开车撞墙活得性快感。”

sentences.en: And I said, "What else?" He said, "Oh, yeah. I told the psychiatrist that I wanted to watch women as they died, because it would make me feel more normal."
sentences.zh: 我说，“还有吗？”他说，“哦对了，我告诉那个精神病专家我喜欢看女人死去因为这让我觉得我比较正常。”

sentences.en: I said, "Where'd you get that from?" He said, "Oh, from a biography of Ted Bundy that they had at the prison library."
sentences.zh: 我说，“你这是从哪学来的？”他说，“哦，从Ted Bundy（连环杀手）的自传监狱图书馆里有这本书。”

sentences.en: Anyway, he faked madness too well, he said.
sentences.zh: 总之，他说他装得太像了

sentences.en: And they didn't send him to some cushy hospital.
sentences.zh: 结果他们没把他送到某间舒适的医院

sentences.en: They sent him to Broadmoor. And the minute he got there, said he took one look at the place, asked to see the psychiatrist, said, "There's been a terrible misunderstanding.
sentences.zh: 反而送到了布罗德莫精神病院他到这里的那一刻他说他看了下四周的环境，然后要求去见精神病医生说，“这当中有着难以解释的误会

sentences.en: I'm not mentally ill." I said, "How long have you been here for?"
sentences.zh: 我并没有任何精神疾病。”我问，“你在这待了多长时间了？”

sentences.en: He said, "Well, if I'd just done my time in prison for the original crime, I'd have got five years.
sentences.zh: 他说，“唉，如果我只在狱中服刑的话我只要待五年

sentences.en: I've been in Broadmoor for 12 years." Tony said that it's a lot harder to convince people you're sane than it is to convince them you're crazy.
sentences.zh: 但我在布罗德莫精神病院已经12年了。”Tony说，要使别人相信你是正常人是十分困难的而使别人相信你疯了则简单得多

sentences.en: He said, "I thought the best way to seem normal would be to talk to people normally about normal things like football or what's on TV.
sentences.zh: 他说，“要显得正常，我觉得最好的方法就是和他人正常地交谈，聊一聊正常的事物像足球或电视上的事情

sentences.en: I subscribe to New Scientist, and recently they had an article about how the U.S. Army was training bumblebees to sniff out explosives.
sentences.zh: 我有订阅《新科学家》这份杂志最近他们发表了一篇文章关于美国军队训练大黄蜂来侦查爆炸物的

sentences.en: So I said to a nurse, 'Did you know that the U.S. Army is training bumblebees to sniff out explosives?'
sentences.zh: 然后我跟护士说你知道美国军队正在训练大黄蜂来侦查爆炸物吗

sentences.en: When I read my medical notes, I saw they'd written: 'Believes bees can sniff out explosives.'"
sentences.zh: 当我看到我的医疗记录时我看到他们写到“相信蜜蜂能侦查爆炸物”

sentences.en: (Laughter) He said, "You know, they're always looking out for nonverbal clues to my mental state.
sentences.zh: 他说，“你知道，他们总是在寻找非言语的线索来判断我的心理状态

sentences.en: But how do you sit in a sane way? How do you cross your legs in a sane way?
sentences.zh: 但你是如何用正常人的方式坐的？你又如何用正常人的方式翘脚的？

sentences.en: It's just impossible." When Tony said that to me, I thought to myself, "Am I sitting like a journalist?
sentences.zh: 这简直就是天荒夜谈。”当Tony告诉我这些的时候我心想，“我坐得像个记者吗

sentences.en: Am I crossing my legs like a journalist?"
sentences.zh: 我翘脚翘得像个记者吗？”

sentences.en: He said, "You know, I've got the Stockwell Strangler on one side of me, and I've got the 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips' rapist on the other side of me.
sentences.zh: 他说，“我的邻居一边住着斯托克威尔扼杀者案的凶手另一边住着整天哼唱着踮起脚尖穿过郁金香花丛的强奸犯

sentences.en: So I tend to stay in my room a lot because I find them quite frightening.
sentences.zh: 因为他们其实挺可怕的，所以我大部分时间是在自己房间的

sentences.en: And they take that as a sign of madness.
sentences.zh: 但他们将此当作发疯的征兆

sentences.en: They say it proves that I'm aloof and grandiose."
sentences.zh: 他们说这表明我冷漠并浮夸。”

sentences.en: So, only in Broadmoor would not wanting to hang out with serial killers be a sign of madness.
sentences.zh: 所以只有在这里，不想和连环杀手交往才是发疯的征兆

sentences.en: Anyway, he seemed completely normal to me, but what did I know?
sentences.zh: 总之他对我来说完全正常——但我又知道些什么呢

sentences.en: And when I got home I emailed his clinician, Anthony Maden.
sentences.zh: 当我回到家时我给他的临床医生Anthony Maden发了电邮

sentences.en: I said, "What's the story?" And he said, "Yep. We accept that Tony faked madness to get out of a prison sentence, because his hallucinations -- that had seemed quite cliche to begin with -- just vanished the minute he got to Broadmoor.
sentences.zh: 我问，“这里面有什么故事吗？”他说，“对，我们知道Tony装疯以逃牢狱之灾因为起初他陈述的老掉牙的幻想在他踏入布罗德莫精神病院那刻便了无踪影

sentences.en: However, we have assessed him, and we've determined that what he is a psychopath."
sentences.zh: 但是，我们对他进行了测试所以我们才决定把他诊断为精神病患者

sentences.en: And in fact, faking madness is exactly the kind of cunning and manipulative act of a psychopath.
sentences.zh: 事实上，装疯正是一种精神病患者狡猾和控制欲强的表现行为

sentences.en: It's on the checklist: cunning, manipulative.
sentences.zh: 它就写在检核表上：狡猾且控制欲强

sentences.en: So, faking your brain going wrong is evidence that your brain has gone wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以假装大脑出了问题就是你大脑真的出问题的证据

sentences.en: And I spoke to other experts, and they said the pinstripe suit -- classic psychopath -- speaks to items one and two on the checklist: glibness, superficial charm and grandiose sense of self-worth.
sentences.zh: 然后我又跟其他专家交流了他们说带条纹的西服——典型的精神病患者证明了检核表上的第一和第二项——口若悬河，迷人外表和自恋的浮夸感

sentences.en: And I said, "Well, but why didn't he hang out with the other patients?"
sentences.zh: 我又说，“好吧，那他不想和其他病人来往又怎么说呢？”

sentences.en: Classic psychopath -- it speaks to grandiosity and also lack of empathy.
sentences.zh: 典型精神病患者——这证明了浮夸和缺乏同理心

sentences.en: So all the things that had seemed most normal about Tony was evidence, according to his clinician, that he was mad in this new way.
sentences.zh: 所以那些对于Tony来说都是十分正常的事都是病证，根据他的医生的说法这是一种新型的发疯

sentences.en: He was a psychopath. And his clinician said to me, "If you want to know more about psychopaths, you can go on a psychopath-spotting course run by Robert Hare, who invented the psychopath checklist."
sentences.zh: 他就是个精神病患者然后他的医生又跟我说“如果你想多一些了解精神病患者你可以去参加“观察精神病患者课程”是由发明“病态人格检核表”的Robert Hare授课的

sentences.en: So I did. I went on a psychopath-spotting course, and I am now a certified -- and I have to say, extremely adept -- psychopath spotter.
sentences.zh: 我还真参加了我报名参加了“观察精神病患者课程”现在我是一名持证的不得不说，还挺资深的精神病患者观察员

sentences.en: So, here's the statistics: One in a hundred regular people is a psychopath.
sentences.zh: 这有些数据：100个普通正常人当中就有一个精神病患者

sentences.en: So there's 1,500 people in his room. Fifteen of you are psychopaths.
sentences.zh: 而这个大厅里有1500人所以当中有15个人是精神病患者

sentences.en: Although that figure rises to four percent of CEOs and business leaders, so I think there's a very good chance there's about 30 or 40 psychopaths in this room.
sentences.zh: 并且这个比例会在CEO和商业领导者中上升到4%所以我觉得这是非常难得的机会在这个大厅里约有30到40名精神病患者

sentences.en: It could be carnage by the end of the night.
sentences.zh: 可能在今晚结束的时候会有大屠杀

sentences.en: (Laughter) Hare said the reason why is because capitalism at its most ruthless rewards psychopathic behavior --
sentences.zh: （笑声）Hare解释说原因来自资本主义的冷酷无情造就了精神疾病的行为

sentences.en: the lack of empathy, the glibness, cunning, manipulative.
sentences.zh: 缺乏同理心，口若悬河狡猾，控制欲强

sentences.en: In fact, capitalism, perhaps at its most remorseless, is a physical manifestation of psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，或许冷酷无情的资本主义正是精神疾病的物质表现

sentences.en: It's like a form of psychopathy that's come down to affect us all.
sentences.zh: 这也是精神疾病的一种形式归根到底会影响着我们

sentences.en: Hare said, "You know what? Forget about some guy at Broadmoor who may or may not have faked madness.
sentences.zh: Hare还跟我说，“你知道吗？别再想布罗德莫精神病院里哪个可能装疯，哪个是真疯谁在乎呢？那并不重要，

sentences.en: Who cares? That's not a big story. The big story," he said, "is corporate psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，”他接着说，“是企业型变态人格

sentences.en: You want to go and interview yourself some corporate psychopaths."
sentences.zh: 你可以亲自去采访一些'企业里的精神病患者'。”

sentences.en: So I gave it a try. I wrote to the Enron people.
sentences.zh: 所以我就试了下。我给安然公司（Enron）写了信我说，“我能来你们这并在狱中采访下你们

sentences.en: I said, "Could I come and interview you in prison, to find out it you're psychopaths?"
sentences.zh: 看看你们是不是精神病患者吗？”

sentences.en: (Laughter) And they didn't reply. (Laughter) So I changed tack.
sentences.zh: 之后就杳无音讯了所以我换了另一种方式

sentences.en: I emailed "Chainsaw Al" Dunlap, the asset stripper from the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 我电邮了“杀手艾尔”Dunlap90年代开始的资产掠夺者

sentences.en: He would come into failing businesses and close down 30 percent of the workforce, just turn American towns into ghost towns.
sentences.zh: 他能让企业倒闭并失去30%的劳动力他能将美国的城镇变成荒凉之地

sentences.en: And I emailed him and I said, "I believe you may have a very special brain anomaly that makes you ... special, and interested in the predatory spirit, and fearless.
sentences.zh: 所以我给他发了电邮说道“我相信您有一颗独特异常的大脑使您变得如此出众您崇尚掠夺精神并且无所畏惧

sentences.en: Can I come and interview you about your special brain anomaly?"
sentences.zh: 那我能采访下您关于你那颗特别独特的大脑吗？”

sentences.en: And he said, "Come on over!" (Laughter) So I went to Al Dunlap's grand Florida mansion.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，“过来吧。”所以我去了他佛罗里达的大豪宅

sentences.en: It was filled with sculptures of predatory animals.
sentences.zh: 到处都是食肉动物的雕塑

sentences.en: There were lions and tigers -- he was taking me through the garden -- there were falcons and eagles, he was saying, "Over there you've got sharks and --" he was saying this in a less effeminate way -- "You've got more sharks and you've got tigers."
sentences.zh: 还有狮子和老虎他带着我穿过花园那儿有猎鹰和老鹰他跟我说，“在那儿你能看到鲨鱼。”他说这话的语气还挺霸气的“你还会看到更多的鲨鱼和老虎”

sentences.en: It was like Narnia. (Laughter) And then we went into his kitchen.
sentences.zh: 那里就像纳尼亚王国（笑声）之后我们来到他的厨房

sentences.en: Now, Al Dunlap would be brought in to save failing companies, he'd close down 30 percent of the workforce.
sentences.zh: 现在Al Dunlap会被聘请去拯救那些濒临破产的公司他会将劳动力减少30%

sentences.en: And he'd quite often fire people with a joke.
sentences.zh: 他经常会用开玩笑的口吻炒别人鱿鱼

sentences.en: Like, for instance, one famous story about him, somebody came up to him and said, "I've just bought myself a new car."
sentences.zh: 举个例子，一个关于他的经典传闻有人找到他，跟他说，“我刚给自己买了新车。”

sentences.en: And he said, "Well, you may have a new car, but I'll tell you what you don't have -- a job."
sentences.zh: 他说，“你或许有了一辆新车，但我告诉你，你没有的，是一份工作。”

sentences.en: So in his kitchen -- he was in there with his wife, Judy, and his bodyguard, Sean -- and I said, "You know how I said in my email that you might have a special brain anomaly that makes you special?"
sentences.zh: 话说在厨房——他正和妻子Judy站在一起还有他的保镖Sean，然后我会说，“你记得我在电邮里写的关于你有一颗让你出众的独特奇异的大脑吗？”

sentences.en: He said, "Yeah, it's an amazing theory, it's like Star Trek.
sentences.zh: 他说，“记得，这说法还真不赖感觉就像《星际迷航》一样。现在还没人做到像你这样。”

sentences.en: You're going where no man has gone before."
sentences.zh: 你要去的地方以前没有人去过。”

sentences.en: And I said, "Well --" (Clears throat) (Laughter) Some psychologists might say that this makes you --" (Mumbles) (Laughter) And he said, "What?"
sentences.zh: 然后我又说，“其实，一些心理学家或许会说这颗大脑让你变成...”（ 喃喃而语）（笑声）他紧接着问，“啥？”

sentences.en: And I said, "A psychopath." And I said, "I've got a list of psychopathic traits in my pocket.
sentences.zh: 我说，“一个疯子。”我接着说，“我口袋里有张清单列举了些精神病患特征

sentences.en: Can I go through them with you?" And he looked intrigued despite himself, and he said, "Okay, go on."
sentences.zh: 我能和你将这些过一遍吗？”尽管他自己看起来很迷惑但他还是说，“行，继续。”

sentences.en: And I said, "Okay. Grandiose sense of self-worth."
sentences.zh: 我说，“那开始吧。自我价值的浮夸感。”

sentences.en: Which I have to say, would have been hard for him to deny, because he was standing under a giant oil painting of himself.
sentences.zh: 就这个，我得说，他还挺难去否认的因为他就站在一幅巨大的油画自画像下面

sentences.en: (Laughter) He said, "Well, you've got to believe in you!"
sentences.zh: （笑声）他说，“好吧，你总要相信自己对吧！”

sentences.en: And I said, "Manipulative." He said, "That's leadership."
sentences.zh: 我又接着，“控制欲强。”他说，“这叫领导能力。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) And I said, "Shallow affect, an inability to experience a range of emotions."
sentences.zh: 我接着，“淡化影响：无法承受一系列的情绪波动

sentences.en: He said, "Who wants to be weighed down by some nonsense emotions?"
sentences.zh: 他说，“谁又想被无意义的情绪波动给压倒呢？”

sentences.en: So he was going down the psychopath checklist, basically turning it into "Who Moved My Cheese?"
sentences.zh: 接着他过了一遍精神病检核表基本和《谁动了我的奶酪》里面一样（为自己辩解）

sentences.en: (Laughter) But I did notice something happening to me the day I was with Al Dunlap.
sentences.zh: （笑声）但我确实觉察到和Al Dunlap在一起的那天发生的一些事

sentences.en: Whenever he said anything to me that was kind of normal -- like he said "no" to juvenile delinquency, he said he got accepted into West Point, and they don't let delinquents in West Point.
sentences.zh: 无论他说什么，我听起来都觉得挺正常的就像他反对少年违法犯罪一样他说他被西点军校（West Point）录取了在西点军校是不允许有过失的

sentences.en: He said "no" to many short-term marital relationships.
sentences.zh: 他反对很多短期的婚姻关系

sentences.en: He's only ever been married twice. Admittedly, his first wife cited in her divorce papers that he once threatened her with a knife and said he always wondered what human flesh tasted like, but people say stupid things to each other
sentences.zh: 他只结过两次婚无可否认，他第一任妻子是在他拿刀威胁下才在离婚协议上签字的他妻子说他一直很好奇人肉尝起来是怎样的但人们总会在失败的婚姻争吵中说些傻话

sentences.en: in bad marriages in the heat of an argument, and his second marriage has lasted 41 years.
sentences.zh: 而他的第二段婚姻持续了41年

sentences.en: So whenever he said anything to me that just seemed kind of non-psychopathic, I thought to myself, well I'm not going to put that in my book.
sentences.zh: 所以无论他说什么，我听起来都不觉得他有精神病我心想，好吧，我不打算把这些写进书里

sentences.en: And then I realized that becoming a psychopath spotter had kind of turned me a little bit psychopathic.
sentences.zh: 但之后我意识到成为一个精神病患观察员倒是让我变得有点神神颠颠的

sentences.en: Because I was desperate to shove him in a box marked "Psychopath."
sentences.zh: 因为我拼命想证明他是神经病患者

sentences.en: I was desperate to define him by his maddest edges.
sentences.zh: 我拼命想用他最疯狂的举动来判定

sentences.en: And I realized, my God -- this is what I've been doing for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 突然我意识到，天啊，我干这都干了20年了记者就都是做这些啊

sentences.en: It's what all journalists do. We travel across the world with our notepads in our hands, and we wait for the gems.
sentences.zh: 我们带着笔记本走遍世界等待着劲爆的料子

sentences.en: And the gems are always the outermost aspects of our interviewee's personality.
sentences.zh: 而所谓的料子却总是那些和被采访人的人格相差得十万八千里的花边

sentences.en: And we stitch them together like medieval monks, and we leave the normal stuff on the floor.
sentences.zh: 我们像中世纪僧侣（文化智慧的象征）将他们联系起来却把那些正常的方面抛掷脑外

sentences.en: And you know, this is a country that over-diagnoses certain mental disorders hugely.
sentences.zh: 而这正是一个大量过度诊断精神疾病的国家

sentences.en: Childhood bipolar -- children as young as four are being labeled bipolar because they have temper tantrums, which scores them high on the bipolar checklist.
sentences.zh: 儿童双相障碍症——约4岁的儿童被诊断为双相障碍症因为他们脾气暴躁这在双相障碍症的检核表上位居榜首

sentences.en: When I got back to London, Tony phoned me.
sentences.zh: 当我回到伦敦时，Tony给我打了电话

sentences.en: He said, "Why haven't you been returning my calls?"
sentences.zh: 他说，“你为什么还没给我回电？”

sentences.en: I said, "Well, they say that you're a psychopath."
sentences.zh: 我说，“因为他们说你确实有精神病。”

sentences.en: And he said, "I'm not a psychopath." He said, "You know what?
sentences.zh: 他说，“我没精神病。”

sentences.en: One of the items on the checklist is lack of remorse, but another item on the checklist is cunning, manipulative.
sentences.zh: 他说，“你知道吗，检核表上有一项是缺乏懊悔但另一项却是狡猾，且控制欲强

sentences.en: So when you say you feel remorse for your crime, they say, 'Typical of the psychopath to cunningly say he feels remorse when he doesn't.'
sentences.zh: 所以当你说你对犯罪感到懊悔时他们会说，典型的精神病患者狡猾地欺骗说他感到懊悔，其实不然

sentences.en: It's like witchcraft, they turn everything upside-down."
sentences.zh: 这就像巫术，他们完全颠覆了一切。”

sentences.en: He said, "I've got a tribunal coming up.
sentences.zh: 他说，“我接下来有个裁决

sentences.en: Will you come to it?" So I said okay. So I went to his tribunal.
sentences.zh: 你要来吗？”然后我答应了之后我去了那个裁决

sentences.en: And after 14 years in Broadmoor, they let him go.
sentences.zh: 在布罗德莫精神病院住了14年后，他们总算让他离开了

sentences.en: They decided that he shouldn't be held indefinitely because he scores high on a checklist that might mean that he would have a greater than average chance of recidivism.
sentences.zh: 他们决定说他不应该被无限期拘留因为他在检核表上分数很高这意味着他再犯的几率要比平均数还高

sentences.en: So they let him go. And outside in the corridor he said to me, "You know what, Jon?
sentences.zh: 所以他们让他离开了就在外面的走廊他跟我说“Jon，你知道吗

sentences.en: Everyone's a bit psychopathic." He said, "You are, I am. Well, obviously I am."
sentences.zh: 每个人多少都有精神病。”他说，“你有，我有，显然我是有的。”

sentences.en: I said, "What are you going to do now?" He said, "I'm going to go to Belgium.
sentences.zh: 我说，“那你现在准备干什么呢？”他说，“我打算去比利时

sentences.en: There's a woman there that I fancy. But she's married, so I'm going to have to get her split up from her husband."
sentences.zh: 因为那里有个我喜欢的女人但她结婚了，所以我准备去让她和她丈夫离婚。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Anyway, that was two years ago, and that's where my book ended.
sentences.zh: （笑声）总之，那是两年前的事了也是我书的最后情节

sentences.en: And for the last 20 months, everything was fine.
sentences.zh: 过去的20个月，一切正常

sentences.en: Nothing bad happened. He was living with a girl outside London.
sentences.zh: 安然无恙他和一个女孩住在伦敦以外

sentences.en: He was, according to Brian the Scientologist, making up for lost time, which I know sounds ominous, but isn't necessarily ominous.
sentences.zh: 按照科学论派学者Brian的说法他在弥补失去的时间——我知道这听起来不是好兆头不过也说不定

sentences.en: Unfortunately, after 20 months, he did go back to jail for a month.
sentences.zh: 20个月后，很可惜他又回到监狱里待了一个月

sentences.en: He got into a "fracas" in a bar, he called it.
sentences.zh: 他在酒吧里和别人发生争吵，他是这样说的

sentences.en: Ended up going to jail for a month, which I know is bad, but at least a month implies that whatever the fracas was, it wasn't too bad.
sentences.zh: 所以在监狱里待了一个月我知道这并不好但至少一个月的刑期，说明不管是什么争吵后果应该不算严重

sentences.en: And then he phoned me. And you know what, I think it's right that Tony is out.
sentences.zh: 然后他打电话给我知道吗，我觉得Tony出来是对的

sentences.en: Because you shouldn't define people by their maddest edges.
sentences.zh: 因为你不能单靠人的疯狂举止就去判定他们

sentences.en: And what Tony is, is he's a semi-psychopath.
sentences.zh: 那Tony算什么呢，算半个疯子吧

sentences.en: He's a gray area in a world that doesn't like gray areas.
sentences.zh: 他处在世界上一个不像灰色地带的灰色地带

sentences.en: But the gray areas are where you find the complexity.
sentences.zh: 这个灰色地带是复杂和纠结的聚集地

sentences.en: It's where you find the humanity, and it's where you find the truth.
sentences.zh: 在这你能看到人道也能看到真相

sentences.en: And Tony said to me, "Jon, could I buy you a drink in a bar?
sentences.zh: Tony跟我说“Jon，我能请你去酒吧喝一杯吗？

sentences.en: I just want to thank you for everything you've done for me."
sentences.zh: 我想谢谢你为我所做的一切。”

sentences.en: And I didn't go. What would you have done?
sentences.zh: 但我没去。换做你，你会去吗？

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢（掌声）
